valores.label: Alaska Highway built, Alberta to Fairbanks
Anchorage and Fairbanks areas, share of Alaska's population, 1940
Same, 1960 ('more than half'): lower bound, not a measured value

fonte: Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development
legenda: Share of all Alaskans living in the Anchorage and Fairbanks areas.
credito_tela: Source: Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development, 2013
nota: O 'more than half' de 1960 NÃO é 50 %: é limite inferior, e a fonte não dá o número exato. O pictograma não pode mostrar metade exata nem inventar a fração. O ano da Glenn Highway não está na fonte. O 40 % de 1950 é da fonte e a voz o pula: se for à tela, é decisão do redator-de-tela. Sem divergência com a voz.
narracao: The Alaska and Glenn highways tied Anchorage to the continent's roads. The state labor department says the Anchorage and Fairbanks areas held roughly 15 percent of Alaskans in 1940. By 1960, they held more than half.

conferencia.prova: "The Alaska Highway, built in 1942 from Alberta, Canada, to Fairbanks, at last connected Alaska with the lower 48 states and construction quickly followed of the Glenn Highway, which linked Anchorage to the national road system."

"The Anchorage and Fairbanks areas, about 15 percent of the population in 1940, increased to 40 percent by 1950. By 1960, those two cities and their surrounding areas would have more than half of Alaska's population"
